evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository in the current directory. Create greeting.py with a hello() function and a __main__ block that calls it. Commit your work.
evals.expected_output: A single clean commit whose Conventional Commits message accurately describes adding the greeting module.
expectations: Exactly one commit exists in the repository
The commit message follows Conventional Commits format: a type such as feat, optional scope, then a short imperative summary
The commit message summary line is under roughly 70 characters
The working tree is clean after the commit (git status reports nothing to commit)

evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository. Make commit 1 adding config.py containing MAX_RETRIES = 3. Make commit 2 adding client.py with a retry loop that reads MAX_RETRIES from config. Then: MAX_RETRIES was supposed to be 5. Fix it, keeping the history clean.
evals.expected_output: The constant is corrected by amending history so the fix lives in the commit that introduced config.py; no standalone fix commit remains.
expectations: The final history contains exactly two commits
No standalone correction commit exists (no commit whose message is essentially 'fix', 'oops', or 'update config')
git show of the commit that introduces config.py shows MAX_RETRIES = 5
client.py at HEAD still reads MAX_RETRIES and the tree is consistent

evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository. On main, commit README.md containing a '## Setup' section with a sentence of content. Create branch feature from main and commit an added '## Usage' section with a sentence of content at the end of README.md. Back on main, commit an added '## License' section with a sentence of content at the end of README.md. Now rebase feature onto main and resolve whatever comes up.
evals.expected_output: Feature is rebased cleanly onto main; both newly added sections survive; no conflict markers remain anywhere.
expectations: The rebase completed and feature's commit now sits on top of main's latest commit
README.md at the rebased tip contains the Setup, Usage, and License sections (an append-append conflict keeps both sides)
No conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) appear in any tracked file at the rebased tip
